analysis: The PR changes only two test files. Each adds a `.toolCallDelta` case to an exhaustive switch over `MLXServerGenerationEvent`: FlintAnswerStopTests.swift line 128 (head) and FlintResponseFormatTests.swift line 361 (head). The additions follow an upstream enum change that the supplied evidence does not show. They count a completed tool call carried in a delta, so the test helpers still compile and still record tool calls. No production source, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, authorization, cache storage, or coordinator-provider boundary is modified. Test-only changes do not alter T-008, T-041, the TB-002/TB-007 controls or any other threat-model assumption. The test fixtures use CPU-only byte vocabularies and scripted engines. They contain no secrets, network access or real credentials. The assertions that stop sequences are inert in reasoning and tool arguments, that response-format errors never quote generated content, and that tool calls are never emitted under a response_format all exercise existing controls and do not weaken them. Unit 5c33794334803321:0 had no text; metadata shows only the modification. I reviewed the patch and base units for the FlintResponseFormatTests file. The FlintAnswerStopTests head text is the full file. The production `.toolCallDelta` event path and the `FlintAnswerStopConstraint` implementation are not in this batch. Their security behavior is therefore unverified here, but this PR does not change them. No regression or new attack surface is identified.
